div.div:
āvŏcāmentum , i, n. avoco,
I.a means of diverting from pain, trouble, etc., an alleviation, diversion, relaxation, recreation (post-Aug.): “omnia mihi avocamenta exemit dolor,” Plin. Ep. 8, 23, 1 : “admittere avocamenta,” id. ib. 8, 5, 3 ; id. Pan. 82, 8; App. Mag. p. 498; Lact. Opif. Dei, 18; Arn. adv. Gent. 166.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
